subject: Information Practices
text:
(a) What is Boolean Indexing in Pandas? Give an example of how it is used with a DataFrame.
OR
(b) What are the two main data structures in Pandas? Briefly describe each.
modelAnswer:
(a) Boolean Indexing is a method of selecting data from a Pandas Series or DataFrame by passing a boolean array/condition as the index. Rows where the condition is True are selected; rows where it is False are excluded.

Example:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'Name':['Riya','Aman','Priya'], 'Score':[85,45,90]})
result = df[df['Score'] > 60]  # Boolean indexing
print(result)
# Displays rows where Score > 60

OR

(b) The two main data structures in Pandas are:
1. Series: A one-dimensional labeled array that can hold any data type. It has a single column with an associated index.
2. DataFrame: A two-dimensional labeled data structure (like a table/spreadsheet) with rows and columns, where each column can hold a different data type.
keyPoints: Boolean Indexing: filter data using a True/False condition array.
df[df['col'] > value] is the standard syntax.
Series: 1D labeled array with an index.
DataFrame: 2D labeled table — rows indexed, columns named.

subject: Information Practices
text:

(i) What type of IPR violation has occurred?
(ii) Name any two types of licenses that allow sharing/reuse of content legally.
modelAnswer:
(i) The violation is Copyright Infringement — Anjana's book is protected by copyright, and copying its content without permission violates her exclusive reproduction rights.

(ii) Two licenses that allow legal sharing/reuse:
1. Creative Commons License — allows creators to specify permissions (attribution, non-commercial, share-alike, etc.) for reuse.
2. MIT License (or GNU GPL / Apache License) — an open-source license permitting use, modification, and redistribution with minimal restrictions.
keyPoints: Copyright Infringement: copying protected creative work without permission.
Creative Commons licenses: flexible permissions for sharing creative content.
MIT/GNU GPL/Apache: open-source licenses allowing redistribution and modification.
Both require attribution to the original creator.

subject: Information Practices
text:
Define the following terms as used in relational databases:
(i) Domain
(ii) Tuple
modelAnswer:
(i) Domain: The set of all valid/permissible values that a particular attribute (column) can hold. For example, the domain of an 'Age' column might be integers from 1 to 120.

(ii) Tuple: A single row (record) in a relational table. It is an ordered set of attribute values that represents one entity in the relation. For example, one complete student record (roll number, name, marks) is a tuple.
keyPoints: Domain: set of all allowed values for an attribute/column.
Tuple: a single row/record in a relational table.
A table with n attributes has tuples with exactly n values.
Degree = number of attributes; Cardinality = number of tuples.

subject: Information Practices
text:
(a) Define: (i) Modem (ii) Gateway
OR
(b) Differentiate between Add-ons and Plug-ins for web browsers.
modelAnswer:
(a)(i) Modem (Modulator-Demodulator): A device that converts digital data from a computer into analog signals for transmission over phone lines, and converts incoming analog signals back to digital. It enables internet access via telephone lines.

(ii) Gateway: A network device that connects two networks using different protocols or architectures. It acts as a protocol converter, enabling communication between incompatible networks (e.g., connecting a LAN to the internet).

OR

(b) Add-ons: Extra features added to a web browser to extend its functionality, such as download managers, ad blockers, or password managers. They are generally downloaded and installed separately.

Plug-ins: Software components that extend the browser's ability to process specific content types, such as playing Flash animations, PDFs, or multimedia. They work within the browser to handle content the browser cannot natively display.
keyPoints: Modem: converts digital↔analog signals for ISP communication.
Gateway: connects networks of different protocols — acts as a protocol translator.
Add-ons: enhance browser features (UI/UX tools, utilities).
Plug-ins: handle specific media/content types within the browser.

subject: Information Practices
text:
(a) What is Data Protection? State any two measures to protect personal data.
OR
(b) What is cyber crime? Give two examples.
modelAnswer:
(a) Data Protection: The practice of safeguarding important digital information from corruption, compromise, and loss — ensuring data is secure, private, and available only to authorized users.

Two precautionary measures:
1. Use strong, unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication (2FA).
2. Encrypt sensitive data and use secure protocols (HTTPS, SSL/TLS) for transmission.

OR

(b) Cybercrime: Any illegal or criminal activity involving a computer or network. It can target individuals, businesses, or governments.

Two examples:
1. Phishing — fraudulent emails/messages tricking users into revealing passwords or financial information.
2. Hacking — unauthorized access to computer systems or networks to steal, modify, or destroy data.
keyPoints: Data protection: securing data from unauthorized access, corruption, and loss.
Measures: strong passwords, 2FA, encryption, firewalls, regular backups.
Cybercrime: criminal activity involving computers/networks.
Examples: phishing, hacking, identity theft, ransomware, cyberbullying.

subject: Information Practices
text:
Vikram received an email claiming to be from his bank, asking him to click a link and enter his account details to 'verify his account'. He clicked the link and entered his credentials. His account was later debited without his knowledge.
(i) What type of cyber attack did Vikram fall victim to?
(ii) State two ways such attacks are commonly carried out.
(iii) Under which Act can this crime be reported in India?
modelAnswer:
(i) Vikram fell victim to Phishing — a social engineering attack where fraudulent emails/messages impersonate legitimate organizations to steal sensitive information like passwords and banking credentials.

(ii) Two common methods:
1. Email phishing: Fraudulent emails with urgent messages and links to fake websites that mimic real bank/institution sites.
2. SMS phishing (Smishing): Fake text messages with links or callback numbers requesting personal details.

(iii) This can be reported under the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000, specifically under Section 66C (Identity Theft) and Section 66D (Cheating by personation using computer resources).
keyPoints: Phishing: impersonating a trusted entity to steal credentials.
Common methods: email phishing, SMS smishing, fake social media pages.
IT Act 2000 — Section 66C (identity theft), Section 66D (cheating by personation).
Always verify sender email addresses and never click unsolicited links.

subject: Information Practices
text:
XYZ Technologies is setting up a network in a new building with four departments: Management (15 computers), Development (60 computers), Testing (30 computers), Support (20 computers). Distances: Management–Development 50m, Management–Testing 100m, Management–Support 40m, Development–Testing 60m, Development–Support 80m, Testing–Support 70m. Head office is 300 km away.
(i) Which department should house the main server? Justify.
(ii) Suggest where switches should be placed.
(iii) Suggest a wired medium for connecting computers within a department.
(iv) Name a protocol to securely transfer files to/from the head office server.
(v) What type of network connects the building's departments internally?
modelAnswer:
(i) The Development department (60 computers) should house the main server. It has the largest number of computers, so placing the server there minimizes network traffic and provides faster access for the majority of users.

(ii) A switch should be placed in each of the four departments. Each departmental switch connects all computers within that department. These switches are then interconnected, with the Development department's switch acting as the backbone switch.

(iii) Twisted Pair Cable (Cat5e/Cat6 Ethernet cable) or Optical Fibre Cable for connecting computers within a department. Twisted pair is cost-effective for shorter distances.

(iv) SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) or SSH (Secure Shell) should be used for secure file transfer to the head office, as they encrypt data during transmission.

(v) The building's internal network is a LAN (Local Area Network), as all departments are within the same building/campus.
keyPoints: Server in the department with most computers (Development, 60) for optimal access.
One switch per department; Development switch acts as backbone.
Twisted Pair/Ethernet cable is standard for intra-department wiring.
SFTP/SSH for secure remote file transfer to head office.
Internal network = LAN; 300km head office connection = WAN.

text:
A DataFrame 'Doctor' has columns: DName, Specialization, Experience, Fees. Write Python/Pandas statements for:

subject: Information Practices
text:
(a) State any two characteristics of the Pandas library in Python.
OR
(b) What is Boolean Indexing in Pandas? Give a suitable example.
modelAnswer:
(a) Two characteristics of the Pandas library:
1. Pandas provides two primary data structures — Series (1D) and DataFrame (2D) — that make data manipulation and analysis easy.
2. Pandas handles missing data gracefully using NaN (Not a Number) and provides methods like fillna(), dropna() to deal with missing values.

OR

(b) Boolean Indexing is filtering data from a Pandas object (Series/DataFrame) based on a boolean condition — rows where the condition is True are selected; where False are excluded.

Example:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'Student':['Avi','Bea','Cara'], 'Marks':[72, 88, 65]})
print(df[df['Marks'] >= 75])  # Boolean Indexing
# Displays only rows where Marks ≥ 75
keyPoints: Pandas characteristics: 1D/2D data structures, NaN handling, label-based indexing, fast I/O.
Boolean Indexing: filter with True/False condition array.
df[df['col'] condition] syntax selects matching rows.
Result is a new DataFrame containing only matching rows.

(ii) Tuple: A single row in a relational database table representing one complete record (entity). For example, one employee's complete data (EmpID, Name, Department, Salary) is one tuple.
keyPoints: Domain: pool of valid values an attribute can take.
Tuple: one complete row/record in a relation.
Cardinality = number of tuples; Degree = number of attributes.

subject: Information Practices
text:
(a) Define: (i) Modem (ii) Gateway
OR
(b) Differentiate between Add-ons and Plug-ins in the context of web browsers.
modelAnswer:
(a)(i) Modem: A device that converts digital data to analog signals (modulation) for transmission over phone lines, and converts incoming analog signals back to digital (demodulation). It enables broadband/dial-up internet access.

(ii) Gateway: A network node that connects two networks using different communication protocols. It translates between protocols, allowing otherwise incompatible networks to communicate (e.g., a router connecting a home LAN to the internet).

OR

(b) Add-ons: Extensions that add new features or functionality to a web browser beyond its built-in capabilities (e.g., ad blockers, password managers, download accelerators). They enhance the browser's user interface and features.

Plug-ins: Software components installed in a browser to handle specific content types that the browser cannot natively process (e.g., Adobe Flash, PDF viewer). They extend the browser's ability to render or play specific media.
keyPoints: Modem: modulates digital→analog and demodulates analog→digital.
Gateway: protocol translator connecting two different networks.
Add-ons: extend browser features/UI.
Plug-ins: enable browsers to handle specific media/content types.

subject: Information Practices
text:
My Solutions Pvt. Ltd. is setting up offices in Mysuru (HR=30, Research=80, Design=50, TechSupport=20 computers) and Chennai (35 computers). Distances in Mysuru: HR–Research 80m, HR–Design 60m, HR–TechSupport 100m, Research–Design 40m, Research–TechSupport 120m, Design–TechSupport 50m.
(i) Suggest the most suitable department to place the server in Mysuru. Justify.
(ii) Suggest the cable layout for each department using Star topology.
(iii) Which department's switch should be used as the backbone in Mysuru?
(iv) What kind of network connects the Mysuru and Chennai offices? Name the device used.
(v) Name a device suitable to boost signal on long HR–TechSupport link.
modelAnswer:
(i) The server should be placed in the Research department (80 computers — the highest count). Placing it there minimizes total cabling/traffic and provides fastest access for the largest group of users.

(ii) Star topology cable layout: Each department has its own switch (central node). All computers within a department connect directly to that department's switch with individual cable runs — this forms a star pattern per department.

(iii) The Research department's switch should serve as the backbone switch for the Mysuru campus, since it has the most computers (80). All other departmental switches (HR, Design, TechSupport) connect to the Research switch.

(iv) The Mysuru–Chennai connection is a WAN (Wide Area Network) since the two offices are in different cities. A Router is the device used to connect the two offices over the WAN.

(v) A Repeater should be installed on the HR–TechSupport link (100m is relatively long within the campus). The repeater regenerates and amplifies the signal to prevent degradation over the long cable run.
keyPoints: Server: Research dept (80 computers — maximum).
Star topology: each computer connects directly to a central switch per department.
Backbone switch: Research (highest usage); other switches connect to it.
WAN connects Mysuru–Chennai; Router enables inter-city communication.
Repeater: regenerates/amplifies signal on long cable runs.

subject: Information Practices
text:
A Scholarship DataFrame has 5 rows. Write Python/Pandas statements for:
(I) Create the DataFrame using a dictionary-of-Series method.
(II) Rename row indexes to ['a','b','c','d','e'].
(III) Drop the last row from the DataFrame.
modelAnswer:
import pandas as pd

# (I) Create using dictionary of Series
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Name':    pd.Series(['Avi','Bea','Cara','Dev','Eva']),
    'Score':   pd.Series([85, 72, 90, 68, 95]),
    'Amount':  pd.Series([5000, 3000, 8000, 2000, 10000])
})

# (II) Rename row indexes to ['a','b','c','d','e']
df.index = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e']

# (III) Drop the last row
df.drop(df.index[-1], inplace=True)
# OR:
# df = df.iloc[:-1]
keyPoints: pd.DataFrame({'col': pd.Series([...])}) creates from dict of Series.
df.index = [labels] reassigns all row index labels.
df.drop(df.index[-1]) drops the last row by label; df.index[-1] is the last label.
df.iloc[:-1] is an alternative — selects all rows except the last.
